text:
J.T. Miller went back to Vancouver on Nov. 13 and heard it. The boos caught him off guard, according to Vancouver Hockey Daily, and Blue Line Station wrote that he fully embraced the role of villain. The Rangers won that night, which probably helped. It was a reminder of how much of his career happened out west: 404 games as a Canuck before the trade back to New York.

On the ice he has been better than his scoring line suggests. He has 5 goals on 7.93 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and the Rangers have scored 7.9 fewer goals than expected with him out there. Meanwhile, with Miller on at five on five, New York takes 62.8% of the expected goals, which is dominant, and he's on a four-game point streak (1 goal, 5 assists). Evolving-Hockey saw the same pattern last season: 0.9 expected wins against -0.2 actual. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him a setup man, 8.6 primary shot assists per 60. Goals usually follow chances like these, and our numbers project about 67 points.
headline: J.T. Miller is better than his goal total
